entries.title: Alfred Schutz
takeaways: Alfred Schutz (b. 1899, d. 1959), more than any other phenomenologist, attempted to relate the thought of Edmund Husserl to the social world and the social sciences.
His 1932 Der Sinnhafte Aufbau der sozialen Welt supplied philosophical foundations for Max Weber's sociology and the social sciences.

entries.title: Kukla to Leibniz University Hannover
takeaways: Their recent books include Sex Beyond ‘Yes!’: Pleasure and Agency for Everyone (2025) and City Living: How Urban Spaces and Urban Dwellers Make One Another (2021).
At LUH, Kukla will be working on their ERC-funded project, TERRAINS: Territory, Agency, and Inhabiting Space , the details of which (including open positions) can be found here .

In addition to their new position as Chair in Social Philosophy of Science and Language, at LUH Kukla is also a Humboldt Visiting Researcher as well as an affiliate of the SOCRATES Centre for Advanced Studies .

entries.title: The SEP: from Two Files to the “Preëminent Reference Work of Philosophy”
takeaways: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (SEP) gets its own profile in The New Yorker today. .
The profile ‘s author, Sheon Han , writes about how he “laughed in disbelief” when, years ago as an undergraduate, he learned of the SEP.
And while we’re on the subject, don’t forget about this browser plug-in for the SEP which improves the user experience in several ways.

entries.title: The Contents of Perception
takeaways: In contemporary philosophy, the phrase 'the contents of perception' means, roughly, what is conveyed to the subject by her perceptual experience.
There will be a way these things look to you when you see them: they will look to have a certain shape, color, texture, and arrangement relative to one another, among other things.
Your visual experience conveys to you that the piano has these features.
